items.explanation: The religious right mobilized around abortion, gay marriage, and cases like Terri Schiavo's — cutting taxes for the wealthy was the fiscal conservatives' cause, not theirs.
options: A. A constitutional ban on gay marriage
B. Limits on abortion
C. Income-tax cuts for the wealthy
D. Saving Terri Schiavo's life
items.stem: Which was NOT a major goal of the religious right?

option_explanations.A: A constitutional ban on gay marriage really was a major goal of the religious right — it mobilized voters in 2004. This is not the exception.
option_explanations.B: Limits on abortion really were a major goal — the defining cause of the religious right. This is not the exception.
option_explanations.C: Correct — this is the exception. Income-tax cuts for the wealthy were the fiscal conservatives' cause, not the religious right's. The religious right mobilized around abortion, gay marriage, and cases like Terri Schiavo's.
option_explanations.D: Saving Terri Schiavo's life really was a religious-right cause — the 2005 end-of-life case drew massive mobilization. This is not the exception.

items.explanation: Kerry was wounded by his antiwar testimony, his Iraq War vote flip-flop, and ballot measures on gay marriage that turned out conservatives — but his debate performances were widely judged strong.
options: A. His Vietnam-era antiwar statements
B. His voting record on the Iraq War
C. His performance in the 2004 debates
D. State ballot measures on social issues
items.stem: All of the following hurt John Kerry in 2004 EXCEPT

option_explanations.A: Kerry's Vietnam-era antiwar statements really did hurt him — the Swift Boat campaign made his 1971 testimony a liability. This was a real wound, not the exception.
option_explanations.B: Kerry's voting record on the Iraq War really did hurt him — the 'I voted for it before I voted against it' flip-flop. This was a real wound, not the exception.
option_explanations.C: Correct — this is the exception. Kerry's debate performances in 2004 were widely judged strong — the debates were his bright spot, not his weakness.
option_explanations.D: State ballot measures on social issues really did hurt him — gay-marriage bans turned out conservative voters in key states. This was a real wound, not the exception.

items.explanation: Bush echoed Wilson's moral language -- the Fourteen Points' call to spread democracy and the 'Freedom Agenda' -- but the comparison breaks on methods. Wilson built democracy promotion into international institutions like the League of Nations; Bush bypassed the United Nations and invaded Iraq in a preventive war. Same vocabulary, different machinery.

option_explanations.A: Bush did not continue Wilson's methods. Wilson built democracy-spreading into international institutions -- the League of Nations and collective security -- while Bush bypassed the United Nations and waged preventive war in Iraq. Identical goals and methods is an overgeneralization.
option_explanations.B: Wilson did send American troops abroad -- Veracruz in 1914, Haiti in 1915, the Dominican Republic in 1916, and Siberia in 1918. The claim cannot fail on non-interventionism because Wilson was not a non-interventionist.
option_explanations.C: Bush invoked democracy repeatedly to justify the Iraq War -- his 'Freedom Agenda' made spreading democracy the moral center of the war's public case. He never avoided that language.
option_explanations.D: Correct. The rhetoric matches -- both presidents made spreading democracy the moral center of their foreign policy -- but the methods diverge: Wilson worked through international institutions like the League of Nations, while Bush waged unilateral preventive war in Iraq without United Nations authorization.

options: A. The claim is entirely correct: Bush simply continued Wilson's foreign policy, identical in both its democratic goals and its methods of achieving them in every part of the world
B. The claim fails because Wilson refused to send American troops into any foreign country, ruling out any parallel with Bush
C. The claim fails because Bush never invoked the spread of democracy to justify the invasion of Iraq
D. The claim needs qualifying: Bush borrowed Wilson's language of democracy, but Wilson worked through international institutions while Bush waged unilateral preventive war
items.stem: A historian claims George W. Bush's democracy agenda in the Middle East was a direct continuation of Wilsonian internationalism. Which of the following best evaluates the historian's claim?

items.explanation: Delivered weeks after September 11, Giuliani's remarks were a call for resolve at home and abroad — framing the attacks as beyond any political justification so that a forceful response would command broad support. A mayor's speech carries no legal authority, and the Iraq decision came eighteen months later.

option_explanations.A: Iraq was invaded in 2003, eighteen months after these remarks, under a separate 2002 congressional authorization — and a New York mayor's speech is not a legal brief and cannot authorize a war. The timing and the authority are both wrong.
option_explanations.B: Giuliani demanded that terrorists and their sponsors be held to account — he did not call for ending diplomacy with every foreign nation. The speech rejects excuses for terrorism, not foreign relations in general.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Giuliani is framing the attacks as beyond any political excuse — 'there was no excuse for mass murder' — precisely to unite the public and other nations behind a forceful response. The remarks are persuasion, not law.
option_explanations.D: Speakers in September 2001 addressed the living — fellow citizens and world leaders — not historians of the future. Historians use the remarks as evidence today, but that was not their purpose.

options: A. they functioned as a legal brief that gave Congress the legal authority it needed to approve the invasion of Iraq
B. they prove Giuliani opposed any diplomacy with any foreign nation
C. they were meant to rally support for a forceful response by placing terrorism beyond any political excuse
D. they were addressed mainly to future historians studying the September 11 attacks

items.stimulus:
Questions 6–8 refer to the following excerpt (paraphrased).

Speaking after the September 11 attacks, New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani declared there was no excuse for mass murder — that terrorists who slaughter innocent civilians place themselves outside civilization, and that America would hold them and their sponsors to account.
—After Mayor Rudy Giuliani's remarks, September 2001

items.explanation: Days after September 11, Congress passed the Authorization for Use of Military Force against those responsible -- the legal foundation for the Afghanistan campaign and much that followed. The Iraq invasion came eighteen months later under a separate 2002 authorization; defense spending rose, and the CIA was expanded, not abolished.
options: A. declared war on Iraq immediately
B. cut the American defense budget
C. abolished the Central Intelligence Agency
D. authorized military force against those responsible for the attacks
items.stem: In response to the September 11 attacks, Congress
items.stimulus:
Questions 6–8 refer to the following excerpt (paraphrased).

Speaking after the September 11 attacks, New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani declared there was no excuse for mass murder — that terrorists who slaughter innocent civilians place themselves outside civilization, and that America would hold them and their sponsors to account.
—After Mayor Rudy Giuliani's remarks, September 2001

option_explanations.A: Congress did not declare war on Iraq immediately after 9/11 — the Iraq invasion came eighteen months later under a separate 2002 authorization. The immediate response was the AUMF against those responsible for the attacks.
option_explanations.B: Congress did not cut the defense budget after 9/11 — defense spending rose sharply. Cuts were the opposite of what happened.
option_explanations.C: Congress did not abolish the CIA — the agency was expanded and given new counterterrorism powers. Abolition was never on the table.
option_explanations.D: Correct. Days after September 11, Congress passed the Authorization for Use of Military Force against those responsible — the legal foundation for the Afghanistan campaign and much that followed.
